preconditions.description: The input is a single integer k where 1 ≤ k ≤ 10^9.

postconditions.expression: all(line.strip() in ['N', 'Y'] * n for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:]) and all(line == line[::-1] for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:]) and all(line[i] == 'N' for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:] for i in range(n) if i == 0) and any(line[1] == 'Y' for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:])
postconditions.description: The output is a valid adjacency matrix for an undirected simple graph with n vertices (2 ≤ n ≤ 1000), where 'N' means no edge and 'Y' means an edge exists. The diagonal is all 'N', and the matrix is symmetric.

postconditions.expression: n == int(stdout.splitlines()[0].strip()) and n >= 2 and n <= 1000
postconditions.description: The first line of the output is an integer n (2 ≤ n ≤ 1000) representing the number of vertices.

postconditions.expression: len(stdout.splitlines()) == n + 1 and all(len(line.strip()) == n for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:])
postconditions.description: The adjacency matrix has exactly n rows and n columns.

postconditions.expression: any('Y' in line.strip() for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:]) and any('Y' in line.strip() for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:][1:])
postconditions.description: There exists at least one path between vertex 1 and vertex 2 (i.e., there is a 'Y' in row 1 and column 2 or vice versa, or a path exists through intermediate vertices).

postconditions.expression: k == int(stdin.strip()) and (lambda: (lambda G: (lambda d: (lambda paths: sum(1 for _ in paths))(sum(1 for p in product(*[range(1, n + 1) for _ in range(2)]) if p[0] != p[1] and G[p[0] - 1][p[1] - 1] == 'Y' and d[p[0] - 1] + 1 == d[p[1] - 1] and d[p[1] - 1] == min(d[p[0] - 1] + 1, d[p[1] - 1]))(defaultdict(lambda: float('inf'), {0: 0}))(G))))([line.strip() for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:]]))
postconditions.description: The number of shortest paths between vertex 1 and vertex 2 in the constructed graph is exactly equal to the input k. The graph is constructed such that the shortest path length is 2 (i.e., paths of length 2 are the only shortest paths).
